title: 0552-empirical-parameterization-of-the-elo-rating
universal_lens: The Elo rating system is a discrete-time dynamical system where the state transition operator depends on an experience-dependent learning rate. The empirical parameterization replaces heuristic constants with data-driven optimization of a stepwise K-function, maximizing the predictive accuracy of a logistic classifier over rating differences.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats the latent skill parameters as random variables updated via Bayesian inference. The empirical tuning protocol maps to maximum likelihood estimation of hyperparameters in a hierarchical model, where the K-factor schedule governs the variance of the process noise in the latent skill evolution.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the rating difference serves as a sufficient statistic for situational advantage. The experience-based K-function modulates the state-transition kernel, allowing the engine to dynamically adjust belief updates based on agent tenure, thereby capturing non-stationary performance dynamics in real-time decision environments.

primitives.name: Experience-Sensitive Learning Rate Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: 1): K_i = K_a if n_i ≤ n_{c1}; K_b if n_{c1} < n_i ≤ n_{c2}; K_c if n_i > n_{c2}, where n_i = games played by player i.
primitives.latex: K_i(n_i) = \begin{cases} K_a & \text{if } n_i \le n_{c1} \\ K_b & \text{if } n_{c1} < n_i \le n_{c2} \\ K_c & \text{if } n_i > n_{c2} \end{cases}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: K_i: dimensionless learning rate scaling factor; n_i: integer count of games played (dimensionless); K_a, K_b, K_c: dimensionless stepwise rate constants; n_{c1}, n_{c2}: integer game-count cutoff thresholds.
primitives.assumptions: Player adaptation and volatility decrease monotonically with cumulative experience; piecewise constant approximation adequately captures the continuous decay of learning rates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when experience proxies (e.g., game counts) are decoupled from true skill acquisition due to varying competition quality or rest periods; singularities arise if K approaches zero prematurely, freezing state updates.

layer2.telemetry: Empirical win-loss record stability across defined experience bins.

primitives.name: Logistic Expected Score Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Expected score: E_A = 1/(1 + 10^{(R_B - R_A)/400}) (logistic performance distribution assumption).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: E_A: dimensionless expected score (probability of winning); R_A, R_B: dimensionless Elo ratings of agents A and B; 400: fixed scaling divisor (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Latent performance fluctuations follow a logistic distribution; the difference in ratings is a sufficient statistic for predicting match outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under extreme rating disparities where the sigmoid saturates completely, rendering further rating updates numerically unstable or uninformative; assumes symmetric performance distributions.

layer2.mapping: Serves as the foundational probabilistic link function in GSE's situational reasoning layer, translating abstract state differentials into actionable win probabilities.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical innovation in this primitive set is the decoupling of the Elo state-transition mechanism from arbitrary heuristic constants. Traditionally, the K-factor is a global scalar, assuming uniform volatility across all agents. By introducing the experience-sensitive K-function, the system models a non-homogeneous Markov process where the transition intensity depends explicitly on the cumulative path length (game count). This creates a piecewise deterministic dynamical system that asymptotically stabilizes as agents gain experience. The logistic performance distribution acts as the observation kernel, mapping the latent state difference to a bounded probability space. The critical duality emerges in the tuning protocol: instead of optimizing a direct loss function on ratings (which is often ill-posed), the authors optimize the hyperparameters of the K-function by maximizing the discriminative power of a downstream logistic classifier. This transforms the unsupervised rating problem into a supervised meta-learning task. The failure mode arises from the lack of temporal isolation; computing ratings on the full history before fitting the classifier introduces severe lookahead bias, effectively leaking future information into the past state estimates. For GSE, adopting this requires strict time-series cross-validation to prevent overfitting to transient team strengths, ensuring the K-decay truly reflects structural learning rather than noise.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework extends Arpad Elo's original 1978 chess rating system, which relied on psychometric assumptions and fixed K-values. It directly inherits the logistic performance distribution from Mosteller and Girshick (1945) and bridges modern machine learning hyperparameter tuning with classical rating theory. The use of a classifier to tune rating parameters echoes recent work in sports analytics by Hvattum and Arntzen (2010), who demonstrated that rating differences are optimal predictors only when the underlying scale is empirically calibrated to the specific sport's variance structure.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The model implicitly constructs a theory of mind for opposing agents by treating their ratings as proxies for latent skill states. The experience-based K-function encodes a prior belief about agent adaptability: novices are highly volatile and rapidly update their internal models (high K), while veterans possess stable, robust strategies (low K). When two agents interact, the system predicts the outcome based on the current divergence of these latent states. However, it assumes agents are rational optimizers within a fixed strategic space, failing to account for deliberate deception, stylistic mismatches, or sudden exogenous shocks (e.g., injuries) that disrupt the smooth decay of the learning rate.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto must be applied against using the in-sample F1-score as the sole validation metric, as it guarantees optimistic bias due to data leakage. Furthermore, the assumption that game count perfectly proxies for experience may collinearly confound with team quality; a rookie on a losing team accumulates games but learns less than a rookie on a championship contender. The GSE implementation must veto any K-schedule that does not incorporate contextual features (e.g., strength of schedule) into the experience binning, preventing the model from mistaking repetitive failure for stabilized expertise.
